about.title: San Gabriel Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: San Gabriel's mix of small retail plazas, restaurants along Valley Boulevard, and residential complexes near Las Tunas Drive and Del Mar Avenue means property owners have a duty to keep walkways, stairs, and parking areas reasonably safe. When they don't, people get hurt on wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting, or unmarked steps. California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it in time. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage from the business can make the difference in whether a claim holds up. LawProactive doesn't handle claims itself — we're a free service that connects injured San Gabriel residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the evidence, and explain your options without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Getting Legal Help Early Matters

items.title: Notice Is the Core Issue
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many San Gabriel businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof of the hazard and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a portion of your damages. An attorney can help present your case fairly despite shared fault arguments.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in San Gabriel?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property in San Gabriel or Los Angeles County is involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible to avoid missing any deadline.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a San Gabriel business?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of exactly what caused the fall — the wet floor, broken tile, or missing signage — before it gets cleaned up or fixed. Ask an employee to note the incident and try to get names of anyone who saw it happen. Many stores along Valley Boulevard and San Gabriel Boulevard have cameras, so requesting that footage be preserved early can matter a lot.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and there's no cost to have your situation reviewed. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
